t: Largest Integer With Given Digit Sum
o: Find the biggest number with at most n digits whose digits sum to s; return −1 if none exists, and 0 when s = 0. Feasibility: the maximum achievable digit sum with n digits is 9n, so s > 9n means −1 (Example 2: 19 > 18). To maximize the numeric value, make the leading digits as large as possible: greedily place min(9, remaining s) at each position from the most significant side, which never breaks feasibility because the leftover sum always fits in the remaining positions (checked upfront that s ≤ 9n). Example 1: n=2, s=9 → place 9 then 0 → 90. Example 3: s=0 → the only option is 0.
k: Existence check: s is achievable iff s ≤ 9n (with s = 0 giving the number 0).
Greedy front-loading (largest digits first) maximizes the numeric value.
Leading zeros simply mean a shorter number, which is allowed by 'at most n digits'.

a.i: Build the answer digit by digit from the most significant position. At each position take d = min(9, s); since we verified s ≤ 9n initially, the residual sum s − d always satisfies s − d ≤ 9·(positions left), so the greedy never gets stuck and clearly yields the lexicographically (hence numerically) largest digit string.
s: For each of the n positions append min(9, s) and subtract it from s.
Convert the digit list to an integer (an all-zero list becomes 0).
a.t: O(n) — one digit appended per position

a.i: The largest number with digit sum s is: write s = 9q + r with 0 ≤ r < 9. Front-loading gives the digit string (r followed by q nines) when r > 0, otherwise q nines. If its length q + (r > 0) exceeds n, no such number exists; otherwise parse it (empty/all-zero string → 0).
s: Compute q = s // 9 and r = s % 9.
Form the string: str(r) + '9'*q if r > 0 else '9'*q.
If the length exceeds n return −1, else return the parsed value (0 for the empty string).
a.t: O(n) — building the digit string dominates

w: The closed-form approach is the one to present first in an interview — it shows the structure immediately — with the positional greedy as an easy-to-defend alternative. Pitfalls: s = 0 must return 0 (not −1 and not an empty string), s > 9n returns −1, and remember 'at most n digits' permits shorter numbers so no special padding is needed. Follow-ups: smallest such integer (greedy from the least significant side, careful with leading zeros), or counting how many integers satisfy the condition (combinatorics / digit DP).
